groups.title: Rendering Models
groups.question: You are choosing how to render a marketing page, a blog, a dashboard behind login and a product page with prices that change daily. Explain the rendering options and what you would pick for each.

followUps.CSR, SSR, SSG and ISR: What is the trade-off between rendering on the server per request and generating HTML ahead of time?
followUps.Hydration: What is a hydration mismatch and what usually causes it?

evidence.text: Client rendering sends a mostly empty page and builds it in the browser with JavaScript.
Server rendering builds HTML for each request, so content is fresh and visible quickly.
Static generation builds HTML ahead of time for speed, and incremental regeneration refreshes it periodically.
Hydration attaches React's event handlers and state to HTML that was rendered on the server.
The first client render must produce the same output as the server.
Values that differ between server and browser, like the current time or random numbers, cause a mismatch.

notEnough: Only saying hydration makes the page interactive.

groups.title: Server Components
groups.question: Your Next.js page shows a product description, reviews from the database and an add-to-cart button. Explain which parts should be server components and which client components.

followUps.Server and client components: Why can a server component read from the database directly but a client component cannot?
followUps.Composition boundaries: How do you keep the interactive part of a page small when a client component wraps server content?

evidence.text: Server components run only on the server and send no JavaScript to the browser.
Because they never reach the browser, they can safely read databases and secrets.
Only parts that need state or event handlers are marked use client.

notEnough: Only saying server components render on the server.

misconceptions.text: Says client components are never rendered on the server.

evidence.text: Client components should be kept small and placed low in the tree.
Server-rendered content can be passed into a client component as children.
That keeps most of the page as server output and only the interactive part as JavaScript.

notEnough: Only saying to use fewer client components.

groups.title: Next.js App Router
groups.question: You are building a Next.js blog with a shared header, slow-loading comments and posts that rarely change. Explain how the App Router structures pages and handles data.

followUps.Routing, layouts and loading UI: How do folders, layouts and loading files work together in the App Router?
followUps.Data fetching and caching: How would you make a blog post page fast but still update when the author edits it?

evidence.text: Folders define the URL routes.
A layout file wraps its child pages and stays in place when navigating between them.
A loading file shows a fallback instantly while that part of the page streams in.
Pages fetch data on the server.
Next.js can cache the result so repeat visits are fast.
The cache can be refreshed on a schedule or on demand, for example when the post is edited.

groups.title: Search and Sharing
groups.question: Your single-page app ranks poorly in search and links shared on social media show no preview. Explain how server rendering and metadata fix this.

followUps.Metadata and SEO: Why do search engines handle server-rendered pages better than client-rendered ones?
followUps.Open Graph and sitemaps: What controls how a link to your page looks when shared, and how do crawlers find all your pages?

evidence.text: Server rendering puts the real content and metadata in the HTML.
A client-rendered page can start as an empty shell that crawlers may not fully run.
Titles, descriptions and canonical URLs tell search engines what each page is.

notEnough: Only saying SSR is good for SEO.

evidence.text: Open Graph tags set the title, description and image shown in link previews.
A sitemap lists the site's pages so crawlers can find them.
These must be in the server-rendered HTML because preview bots usually do not run JavaScript.
